anchor.quote: Let $\alpha$ denote the initial value of an auxiliary register, which may be any value.
so the value $\gamma$ it leaves in the register depends only on the data, not on $\alpha$.

gaps.term: Restoring the register to its starting value
gaps.note: Stage 1 subtracts alpha, so the register holds 0; stage 2 leaves gamma in it. Adding gamma gives 2 gamma (or 0 if read as subtraction), not the starting value alpha. No stage adds alpha back, so the page does not show that the register ends unchanged, which its opening sentence promises.

gaps.quote: Each operation of stage 2 has an inverse, so the reversal undoes the scratch changes and leaves the data in its intended state.
gaps.note: The page does not say what the stage 2 operations are or why each has an inverse, so the reader cannot check that reversing them undoes the scratch changes and restores the data.
